name: google's gift to the cloud
title: google's gift to the cloud
zoomCaption: Based on Google's internal container orchestrator, 'Borg', Kubernetes (often called K8s) was released as an open-source project in 2014. name: coffee-monitoring webcam
title: coffee-monitoring webcam
description: the first webcam was created to monitor a coffee pot.
zoomCaption: In 1991, researchers at the University of Cambridge's Computer Laboratory set up a camera pointed at the Trojan Room coffee pot. They wanted to see if the pot was full before making the trip to the breakroom. The camera provided a 128x128 grayscale image that was eventually broadcast to the web in 1993.

name: the first 'bug'
title: the first 'bug'
description: the first computer bug was an actual moth.
zoomCaption: On September 9, 1947, engineers working on the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth stuck in a relay, which was causing the machine to malfunction. They taped the moth into their logbook with the note: 'First actual case of bug being found.' While the term 'bug' had been used for mechanical flaws before, this popularized it in computing.

name: the first programmer
title: the first programmer
description: ada lovelace is considered the first computer programmer.
zoomCaption: The daughter of Lord Byron, Ada Lovelace was a brilliant mathematician who worked with Charles Babbage on his 'Analytical Engine'. name: confoederatio helvetica
title: confoederatio helvetica
description: the real name of switzerland is confoederatio helvetica.
zoomCaption: Often abbreviated as 'CH', this Latin name translates to 'Helvetic Confederation'. It was chosen to avoid favoring any of the country's four official languages (German, French, Italian, and Romansh). The name refers to the Helvetii, a Celtic tribe that inhabited the Swiss plateau in antiquity.

name: bluetooth's viking heritage
title: bluetooth's viking heritage
description: bluetooth is named after a 10th-century viking king.
zoomCaption: The technology is named after King Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson, who is famous for uniting Scandinavia—just as Bluetooth was designed to unite PC and cellular industries with a short-range wireless link. Even the Bluetooth logo is a combination of the Younger Futhark runes for his initials: ᚼ (Hagall) and ᛒ (Bjarkan).

name: thucydides trap
title: thucydides trap
description: when a rising power threatens to displace an established hegemon, structural stress makes war the statistical norm.
zoomCaption: Coined by political scientist Graham T. Allison in 2012 from ancient Greek historian Thucydides' chronicle of the Peloponnesian War: 'What made war inevitable was the growth of Athenian power and the fear which this caused in Sparta.' A Harvard Belfer Center study analyzed 16 historical cases over the past 500 years where an emerging power rivaled a ruling power—finding that 12 culminated in catastrophic war.
